answer: Sable Routing Depth. Each agent gets a routed position on a trust graph; messages only propagate if they traverse a minimum ledge of distinct, independently routed neighbors. The rule: an identity's weight equals its graph distance from known seeds, not its count. Fabricating N sybils costs N separate routing paths through real relays, each demanding unique bandwidth and latency. A sonnet of fake nodes collapses to one shallow cluster, capping influence. Attacker pays per-path relay rent, not per-identity registration.
